data.narrative:
Andromeda Surgical is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Nick Damiano and Kartik Tiwari, having raised $10M+. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in Biotech & Health, including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Three standard valuation methods were evaluated. Stage-progression analysis was inapplicable: the implied $7.5B valuation (derived from a $3.0B funding-tracker proxy with a 2.5x seed-stage step-up multiplier) exceeds 20x the company's total raised, indicating the base value is unreliable. Peer-median triangulation could not be executed: while 8 same-sector peers exist, zero met narrow filters for stage, adjacent-stage, or valuation-tier alignment; applying an all-sector median would lack specificity. Public-comp anchoring (anchored to a 6.6x P/S median across the three public tickers) was blocked by the absence of target revenue disclosure, standard for private companies.

No triangulated valuation range can be supported by the available data. The analysis highlights material constraints: seed-stage biotech lacks standardized financial reporting, narrow peer sets resist statistical anchoring, and early-stage company metrics (revenue, user growth) remain confidential. Resolution requires either disclosure of Andromeda's revenue or gross margins, or identification of seed-stage peers with disclosed financials sufficient to establish a defensible median.
